title: U.S. House · Virginia's 4th District
area: Virginia's 4th Congressional District (Richmond, Petersburg, and surrounding areas)

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jennifer McClellan advanced unopposed. The Republican Party primary was canceled because no candidates filed; Robert Murray Jr. is the Republican general-election nominee.

summary.text: Jennifer McClellan is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 4th District, elected in a 2023 special election. She previously served in the Virginia Senate and House of Delegates.

background.text: Born in Petersburg, Virginia in 1972; earned a B.A. in English and political science from the University of Richmond and a J.D. from the University of Virginia.
Worked as assistant general counsel with Verizon and as an associate with the law firm Hunton & Williams.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates (District 71, 2006-2017) and the Virginia State Senate (District 9, 2017-2023) before her election to Congress.

positions.summary: Says Congress must reverse the Trump administration tariffs, which she says have raised costs for families.
positions.quote: We must reverse the Trump administration tariffs that have raised the cost of everything from gas to groceries, housing to healthcare, toys to technology, and beyond.

positions.summary: Says Congress must reverse the Medicaid and safety-net cuts in the 2025 budget law and reinstate the enhanced ACA premium tax credits.
positions.quote: We must reverse the largest cuts to our health care and food security safety nets in American history in the Big Ugly Law (HR1) and reinstate the enhanced premium tax credits under the Affordable Care Act

positions.summary: Says she has fought for reproductive freedom without government interference and, as chair of the Abortion Rights and Access Task Force, is continuing that fight nationwide.
positions.quote: I have fought for the past 20 years for reproductive freedom that supports the fundamental decisions of when, whether and how to become a parent and reproductive health decisions to be left to individuals, with providers, and anyone they chose to bring into the conversation, without government interference.

positions.summary: Says Congress must invest in clean and renewable energy generation and reinstate energy efficiency programs.
positions.quote: We must invest in clean and renewable energy generation, which is the fastest, cleanest and cheapest energy we can get on the grid, and reinstate energy efficiency programs that help reduce demand.

positions.summary: Says she would build on a 2026 federal housing law to increase housing supply, including by cutting red tape on construction.
positions.quote: I will build on the success of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passed this year to increase housing supply at lower costs, cut red tape on construction, and stop large institutional investors from buying up single-family homes.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Subcommittees on Communications and Technology and on Energy, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Robert Murray Jr. is the Republican nominee for Virginia's 4th Congressional District.

positions.summary: Says he welcomed the call to end U.S. military aid to Israel, arguing the aid has fueled antisemitism and that U.S. resources should be focused at home.
positions.quote: I celebrated PM Benjamin Netanyahu’s recent support to end U.S. military aid to Israel, because such aid has fueled antisemitism.

positions.summary: Proposes deregulating housing to accelerate construction as a way to lower housing costs.
positions.quote: A better, more sustainable solution is deregulating housing (to accelerate construction)

positions.summary: Proposes shifting tax burdens to corporations and overseas suppliers while ending the individual income tax mandate.
positions.quote: We need to end the IRS mandate for individual income taxes and shift tax burdens to corporations and overseas suppliers.

summary.text: Joan Bell is an independent candidate running in Virginia's 4th Congressional District general election.
